## Summary

No repository existed in the working directory, so I built a self-contained Go reproduction that matches every fact in the report, then wrote the solution.

**Root cause:** The walk increments `OmittedCount` the instant an item fails the fit test. A later floor/escape-hatch branch keeps that same item when `kept == 0`, but never backs out the increment. The inflated total also feeds the derived `reason`/`marker` strings.

**Fix:** Decrement inside the floor branch that keeps the item, guarded against negative, then re-derive reason/marker from the corrected total — rather than moving the increment out of the fit-test path.

**Verified** (`/home/kara/repro/main.go`):
- Invariant `kept + omitted == len(chain)` holds for all 120 combinations post-fix (0 leaks).
- Reverting the one-line decrement leaks exactly **72/120** combinations (budgets 0–8 across 8 chain lengths — precisely the floor-trigger cases).
- Regression examples match: 1-node `omitted=1`→`0`; 4-node `omitted=4` (3 dropped)→`omitted=3`.

Deliverable written to **`/home/kara/solution.md`** with title, root-cause analysis, exact patch, verification output, and a regression test.

signatures.description: A counting walk increments an omission counter at the moment an item fails the fit test, and a later fallback branch (floor/escape hatch) then KEEPS that same item. The counter is never decremented, so a manifest/report states the kept item was dropped: single-node chain reported omitted=1 with the node present, 4-node chain reported omitted=4 with 3 dropped. Fix shape: decrement inside the floor branch that keeps an item (guarded against a negative total) rather than moving the increment, then re-derive the reason/marker strings from the corrected total. Verification that generalizes: assert the invariant kept + omitted == input size across a sweep of budgets, and falsify by reverting the one-line decrement (72 of 120 combinations leak pre-fix, 0 post-fix).
